qt: to the Vice-President of the Commission / High Representative of the Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy Brando Benifei (S&D), Pina Picierno (S&D), Camilla Laureti (S&D), Alessandra Moretti (S&D), Mercedes Bresso (S&D), Achille Variati (S&D), Franco Roberti (S&D), Elisabetta Gualmini (S&D), Beatrice Covassi (S&D) Subject:

On 1 January, a labour court in Bangladesh sentenced 83-year-old Nobel Peace Prize winner and businessman Muhammad Yunus and three other defendants to six months in prison. They remain free on bail pending an appeal but have been convicted of failing to set up a welfare fund for the workers of Grameen Telecom, a company founded by Mr Yonus. This arbitrary conviction, as a result of a campaign of judicial persecution against Mr Yunus, comes mere days before the general elections in Bangladesh and is only the latest example of crackdown against dissent and human rights by the government of Sheikh Hasina, in power since 2009 and opposed to Mr Yunus. Amnesty International has also criticised the Bengali authorities for the unusual haste with which the trial was concluded and the abusive practice of bringing criminal proceedings to judge administrative matters. Can the Vice-President of the Commission / High Representative of the Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy therefore say: 1.
What he can do to secure the release of Muhammad Yunus and the other three defendants?
What he can do to ensure human rights and the rule of law are unequivocally upheld in Bangladesh?
at: EN on behalf of the European Commission (20.2.2024) 1. The EU is closely following the court case against Nobel Peace Prize laureate, Professor Mohammad Yunus. The EU has inquired about the case in exchanges with Bangladeshi authorities. The EU continues to stress that legal proceedings should be transparent and follow due process. Civil society in Bangladesh plays an important role in fostering development and democracy and an open civic space is a precondition for this role. 2. The EU will continue to work with Bangladesh to foster the values of democracy, human rights and the rule of law that underpin relations. There is a dedicated regular dialogue in the biennial EU-Bangladesh Subgroup on Human Rights and Good Governance, which was last held on 18 May 2022. These values are also integrated in the EU-Bangladesh Political Dialogue as well as in other dialogues, for instance on development, trade and labour issues. Bangladesh currently benefits from the Everything But Arms (EBA) scheme. An EBA monitoring mission visited Bangladesh in November 20231 and, alongside the Generalised Scheme of Preferences report and the report on EU Enhanced Engagement with three Everything But Arms beneficiary countries2 issued the same month, it outlined EU expectations in terms of promotion, protection and fulfilment of human rights in Bangladesh. The EU Special Representative on Human Rights visited Bangladesh in July 2023 and addressed a broad range of issues, including civic space. The EU also engages with civil society and human rights defenders in Bangladesh and extends substantial support to them.
1 EU EBA monitoring mission Bangladesh, 12-16 November 2023,

https://www.eeas.europa.eu/delegations/bangladesh/eu-eba-monitoring-mission-bangladesh-12-16-november2023_en?s=164 2 Both reports can be accessed from https://ec.europa.eu/transparency/documentsregister/detail?ref=SWD(2023)360&lang=en. For Bangladesh key concerns are labour rights (compliance with international standards, anti-union discrimination, child and forced labour) and human rights (fundamental freedoms, need to investigate allegations of serious violations, e.g. torture, extra-judicial killings, enforced disappearances).
